findings.failure_path: An old, nonempty, exactly named hardlinked shadow passes the directory-entry filter. checked_shadow then raises BridgeError, which the sweep's OSError handler misses. The error escapes write_shadow and can deny the first PreToolUse of an unrelated new conversation.
findings.smallest_fix: Catch BridgeError around each sweep entry and continue scanning. Retain fail-closed handling for the current conversation's own shadow. Add a stale-hardlink case that asserts the new conversation's normal verdict and unchanged link target.

findings.failure_path: When a stale shadow has no run-lock entry, cleanup proceeds unlocked. A resumed event can create and acquire that lock after the lookup and write fresh content between the sweeper's mtime check and ftruncate. The running hook can then receive an empty transcript.
findings.smallest_fix: Acquire the same run lock as the writer before checking age and truncating, creating it safely if necessary, or skip the entry when its lock is missing. Cover the missing-lock case.

findings.failure_path: For two chunks of the same multi-line range, one can end immediately before a row separator and the next can start immediately after it. Every numbered row passes the containment check even though the canonical newline was never covered. shadow_events then emits Skill for an incomplete stream.
findings.smallest_fix: Include each internal row separator in the byte interval required for that row. Keep the final row's end at the end of its requested range. Add a regression with exactly one separator byte missing.

findings.failure_path: The UTF-8 exception derives the true start from body length. When the reported start is inside a character, a matching body can extend back past that character's leading byte and still pass the comparison. This accepts a misplaced chunk outside the observed host behavior.
findings.smallest_fix: Find the leading byte of the character containing the reported start and allow only that precise back-off. Test a body containing an extra valid byte before the character as well as the legitimate host case.

findings.failure_path: SHOWING_RE searches the entire result before the Partial header is considered. A valid byte chunk that starts mid-row at literal text matching a Showing lines header is dispatched to the wrong parser. If its totals differ, the genuine chunk contributes no evidence.
findings.smallest_fix: Select the first recognized header in the result preamble before examining the body. Add a valid Partial read whose body starts with header-like skill text.

findings.failure_path: The legacy PID pattern accepts Unicode decimal digits and leading zeros. The old writer interpolated os.getpid() in ordinary decimal form, so the sweep can unlink a stale file that was never a legacy temporary file.
findings.smallest_fix: Match the generated PID spelling with [1-9][0-9]* and assert that near-miss filenames survive the sweep.

findings.failure_path: For each accepted chunk, every row scans the merged interval list from the beginning. As disjoint intervals accumulate, replaying fragmented reads repeatedly multiplies row count by interval count while the event holds the conversation lock. The transcript byte cap does not bound this work to the hook deadline.
findings.smallest_fix: Walk the sorted rows and merged spans together with a monotonic interval index. Cover a fragmented range with the same coverage assertions as the contiguous case.

findings.failure_path: The privacy test checks size only after the final Stop. If PreToolUse leaves transcript-derived content on disk, a later Stop can rewrite and clear it before the assertion. The test would pass despite a privacy regression between events.
findings.smallest_fix: Stat the shadow immediately after each bridge invocation and assert the same inode, mode 0600 and zero size before issuing the next event.

findings.failure_path: The test requires the current skill-extraction-workflow document to occupy exactly three chunks. Other cases unpack exactly three spans and depend on a line and a multibyte character occurring near particular offsets. Routine skill edits can break bridge CI without changing bridge behavior.
findings.smallest_fix: Use a synthetic bundled-skill fixture with controlled line lengths and UTF-8 boundaries. Exercise the same shadow_events entry point against that fixture.

findings.failure_path: All chunk tests load one skill. Removing the per-slug interval key would leave them green while two skills with the same requested line range could contribute intervals to each other's coverage.
findings.smallest_fix: Interleave complementary incomplete reads of two synthetic bundled skills and assert that neither loads. Complete one skill and assert that only its event appears.

findings.failure_path: The state helper always deletes TMPDIR after temporarily overriding it. If the runner supplied a private TMPDIR, subsequent tests and child processes in the same suite lose that setting and can use a different temporary directory.
findings.smallest_fix: Scope the override with mock.patch.dict or restore the original value, including the originally-unset case.

findings.failure_path: The plan says the requester explicitly authorized an always-on global Antigravity rule. The quoted request names two bridge fixes. The proposed rule would additionally change delegation, task polling and review behavior for unrelated work on the machine.
findings.smallest_fix: Remove the global-rule deliverable, its scope-table reference and the claim of explicit authorization from this change.

findings.failure_path: The plan and new source-register row say every event supplies a different identity and therefore every edit is denied. The validation record reports that ext4 reused the numeric inode and the baseline initially passed. Publishing the universal claim gives maintainers an incorrect reproduction criterion.
findings.smallest_fix: State in both places that recreating the file can change its observed identity and re-arm the checkpoint. Scope the consecutive denials to the recorded reproduction.

findings.failure_path: The plan labels the full verifier list as run before and after, but the packet provides no candidate-bound outcomes for make test, git diff --check or the npm suite. It also supplies no conclusive adversarial challenge for this runtime change. The recorded focused results cannot establish the repository's landing conditions.
findings.smallest_fix: Record the actual candidate, commands and outcomes in validation.md, marking outstanding checks pending. Attach the independent review and challenge dispositions before claiming readiness.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: Rewriting and truncating the same file preserves the inode on the normal event path. Partial-read accounting can still synthesize a Skill event with a gap between rows or accept a misplaced UTF-8 start offset.

The direct shadow-write path checks the opened descriptor before writing. The sweep has a separate race when the run lock is absent, and its legacy filename pattern admits names the old writer could never generate.
An unsafe stale shadow can send an unrelated conversation into fallback. Fragmented reads also introduce repeated scans of every stored interval for every row on a time-limited hook path.

The tests exercise repeated edits, link refusal, lock contention and corrupted chunk bodies. They miss cross-skill interval isolation and inspect the empty shadow only after the final event. Several tests also depend on the current size and wording of a live skill document.
A valid Partial read can be misclassified when its body contains header-like text. The plan also adds a machine-wide execution policy outside the two bridge fixes in the quoted request.

The old writer can replace a persistent shadow on the next event, so the file format presents no evident rollback barrier. The packet supplies no candidate-bound outcome for the full repository lane or npm package tests.

A stale hardlink belonging to one conversation can cause a new conversation's first tool call to be denied. That verdict describes the current call even though the failure arose while cleaning another conversation.

The validation record itself reports inode reuse on ext4, contradicting the plan and register's claim that the baseline denied every edit. The reported host observations support the sampled format variants. This review used the frozen packet and did not independently rerun those observations or the tests.

Comparing chunk bodies with bundled bytes establishes their contents. The offset adjustment and omission of row separators weaken the separate claim that those bytes cover the stated stream. The suite also leaves the per-skill boundary untested.

The root scope rule applies to the unrequested global configuration deliverable. The quoted contracts require full validation and independent review and challenge before landing. The packet records focused results and an inconclusive plan review, leaving release verification open.
